skill.title: Use ratios to compare quantities
skill.blurb: Compare two or more quantities measured in the same units using a ratio.

siblings.title: Express a ratio part as a fraction of the whole
siblings.blurb: Express one part of a ratio as a fraction of the whole or of another part, e.g. in $2:3$ the first part is $\tfrac{2}{5}$ of the total and $\tfrac{2}{3}$ of the second.

siblings.title: Produce equivalent ratios
siblings.blurb: Produce equivalent ratios by multiplying or dividing all parts by the same number, including finding a missing value, e.g. $2:9 = \square:18$.

siblings.title: Simplify ratios
siblings.blurb: Simplify a ratio to its lowest whole-number terms.

siblings.title: Simplify ratios with different units
siblings.blurb: Simplify a ratio whose quantities have different units by first converting to the smaller unit, e.g. $45$ min $: 2$ h $= 3:8$.

siblings.title: Simplify ratios involving fractions and decimals
siblings.blurb: Simplify ratios containing fractions or decimals to whole-number form, multiplying by a power of $10$ or a common denominator first, e.g. $0.6:2.7 = 2:9$.

dependents.title: Express a ratio part as a fraction of the whole
dependents.blurb: Express one part of a ratio as a fraction of the whole or of another part, e.g. in $2:3$ the first part is $\tfrac{2}{5}$ of the total and $\tfrac{2}{3}$ of the second.

dependents.title: Produce equivalent ratios
dependents.blurb: Produce equivalent ratios by multiplying or dividing all parts by the same number, including finding a missing value, e.g. $2:9 = \square:18$.

dependents.title: Distinguish ratios from rates
dependents.blurb: Explain that ratios compare like units and rates compare different units.

theory.intro: A **ratio** compares two or more quantities measured in the same units. If a case holds $2$ pens and $3$ rulers, write pens : rulers $=2:3$, read "two to three". Order follows the words, so $2:3$ is not the same as $3:2$.
facts: Ratios can compare three or more quantities, e.g. red : blue : green $=2:3:4$.
A ratio tells you how the amounts compare, not how much there is altogether.
steps: Read the quantities named in the question, in the order they are named.
Count how many of each there are.
Write the counts in that same order, separated by colons.

workedExamples.question_text:
A case holds $5$ pens, $8$ rulers and $3$ erasers. Write the ratio of:
(a) pens to rulers
(b) rulers to pens
(c) erasers to pens to rulers
(d) pens to all the stationery.

A tray contains $31$ counters. Of these, $12$ are blue and the rest are red. Write the ratio of:
(a) blue counters to all counters
(b) blue counters to red counters.
A drink has cordial : water $=3:7$. Does this ratio tell you the total amount of drink? Explain.
workedExamples.solution_text:
No. The ratio means $3$ parts of cordial for every $7$ parts of water.
It gives the comparison between the parts, but not the amount in each part.
The total amount of drink is not given.

foundation.question_text:
A box contains $5$ green marbles and $7$ red marbles.
Write the ratio of green marbles to red marbles.

There are $3$ apples and $4$ bananas in a bowl.
Write the ratio of apples to the total number of pieces of fruit.

In a class of $30$ students, $18$ are girls.
Write the ratio of girls to boys.

development.question_text:
Over $14$ days there were $8$ rainy days, $3$ snowy days and the remaining days were fine. These groups do not overlap.
Write the ratio of rainy days to snowy days to fine days.

In a bag, the ratio of red counters to blue counters is $4:7$.
Write the ratio of blue counters to red counters.

The ratio of boys to girls in a class is $5:4$.
Write the ratio of boys to the whole class.

In a fruit bowl, the ratio of apples to all the fruit is $3:8$.
Write the ratio of apples to the fruit that are not apples.

A car park holds $12$ white cars, $9$ red cars and $4$ black cars.
Write the ratio of black cars to red cars to white cars.

mastery.question_text:
Jacob mixes cordial and water in the ratio $1:4$.
He makes a second drink using cordial to water in the ratio $1:5$.
Jenny says the second drink must contain more liquid than the first.
Explain why Jenny is not correct.
mastery.solution_text:
$1:4$ and $1:5$ each compare cordial with water only.
A ratio gives no information about the total amount, so the second drink could be any size — larger, smaller or the same.

mastery.question_text:
In a group there are $2$ boys for every $3$ girls.
Ravi says the ratio of boys to the whole group is $2:3$.
Explain his error and write the correct ratio.
mastery.solution_text:
$2:3$ compares boys with girls, not with the whole group.
$\text{whole group}=2+3=5\text{ parts}$
$\text{boys}:\text{group}=2:5$

mastery.question_text:
Counters are red, blue and green in the ratio $3:4:5$.
Write the ratio of green counters to all the counters that are not green.

questions.question_text:
Jug A holds a drink with cordial : water $=1:4$.
Jug B holds a drink with cordial : water $=1:6$.
Which statement must be true?

options.text: Jug B's drink has more water for each part of cordial.
Jug B holds more liquid than jug A.
options.why: Assumes a ratio tells you the total amount, when it only compares the parts.

options.text: Jug A holds more cordial than jug B.
options.why: Reads the first number as an actual amount of cordial rather than a comparison.

options.text: Jug B's drink tastes stronger than jug A's.
options.why: Treats a larger second part as meaning more cordial, when it means more water.

questions.solution_text:
$1:4$ means $4$ parts of water for each part of cordial.
$1:6$ means $6$ parts of water for each part of cordial.
Jug B has more water per part of cordial; neither ratio says how much liquid is in either jug.

questions.question_text:
What is the ratio of triangles to squares?
There are 4 triangles and 3 squares.

options.why: Uses the square count and total count rather than triangles compared with squares.
Reverses the requested order of triangles to squares.
Uses the total number of shapes as the first ratio term.

questions.solution_text: There are 4 triangles and 3 squares. Therefore the ratio of triangles to squares is $4:3$.
